title: Fake Election Gifts Cost Scam Victims in Taiwan NT$20 Million
summaryZh: 選舉將近，詐團以免費競選贈品行騙，兩個月損失逾2千萬元。
summaryHi: ताइवान में चुनाव से पहले मुफ़्त चुनावी उपहारों के नाम पर ठगी, दो महीनों में NT$2 करोड़ से ज़्यादा का नुकसान।
summaryEs: Con las elecciones cerca, estafadores usan regalos electorales gratis; las pérdidas superan los NT$20 millones.
summaryJa: 選挙を前に無料の選挙グッズを装う詐欺が横行、2か月で被害2千万元超。
summaryKo: 선거를 앞두고 무료 선거 굿즈 사기가 기승, 두 달간 피해액 2천만 대만달러 넘어.
summaryEn: Scammers are using free election gifts to trick people, causing NT$20 million in losses in two months.
paragraphs: As Taiwan heads into local elections in less than three weeks, police are warning the public that fraudsters are exploiting the campaign season. Offers of free election merchandise, from umbrellas to other promotional goods, have become a popular bait for scams.

The Criminal Investigation Bureau (CIB) said on Sunday that election-related fraud had caused losses of NT$20.15 million over the past two months. October accounted for most of that, with 87 cases and NT$19.11 million stolen.

One victim, a teacher in Kaohsiung, responded to a social media post that promised free election items for a shipping fee of just NT$40. After following a transaction link and completing a supposed real-name verification, she was contacted by someone claiming to be the vendor, who said her account had been frozen. A second scammer, posing as a bank employee, then talked her into making 32 online transactions, costing her NT$1.39 million.

In a separate case, a person hoping to get a campaign umbrella was persuaded by a fake customer service agent to scan a QR code and then generate another code for a cardless cash withdrawal. The loss exceeded NT$920,000.

The CIB stressed that genuine transactions never require buyers to verify payments through online banking. Anyone who receives a suspicious link or banking instruction should stop immediately and check with the 165 anti-fraud hotline.
Taiwan will hold local elections in less than three weeks. Some criminals are using the elections to trick people.
The police say people lost NT$20.15 million in election scams in the last two months. In October alone, there were 87 cases.

In one case, a teacher in Kaohsiung saw a post online. It offered free election gifts. She only had to pay NT$40 for delivery. Then a man said her bank account was frozen. Another man said he worked for a bank. He told her to use online banking many times. She lost NT$1.39 million.
Another person wanted a free election umbrella. A fake helper told the person to scan a QR code. The person lost more than NT$920,000.
The police say a real shop never asks you to check a payment with online banking. If something feels strange, stop. Call 165 for help.

paragraphs: With local elections less than three weeks away, Taiwan's police are warning voters about a new kind of scam. Criminals are using election gifts, such as free umbrellas and other campaign items, to trick people out of their money.

According to the Criminal Investigation Bureau (CIB), victims have lost NT$20.15 million to election-related fraud over the past two months. In October alone, there were 87 cases, with losses of NT$19.11 million.

In one case, a teacher in Kaohsiung saw a social media post offering free election products for a NT$40 delivery fee. After she clicked a link and did a so-called real-name check, someone pretending to be the seller said her account was frozen. A second person, posing as a bank worker, then guided her through 32 online transfers. She lost NT$1.39 million.

In another case, a person who wanted a campaign umbrella was told by a fake customer service worker to scan a QR code. The victim then made a code for a cash withdrawal without a card and lost more than NT$920,000.
The police say real sellers never ask buyers to confirm payments through online banking. If a strange link or bank request appears, people should stop at once and call the 165 anti-fraud hotline.

paragraphs: With Taiwan's local elections now less than three weeks away, police have warned that fraudsters are capitalising on the campaign season, using the lure of free election merchandise to lead unsuspecting people into elaborate banking scams.

Figures released by the Criminal Investigation Bureau (CIB) on Sunday show that election-related fraud has cost victims NT$20.15 million over the past two months. The bulk of the damage came in October, when 87 cases resulted in losses of NT$19.11 million.

In one typical case, a Kaohsiung teacher came across a social media post offering free campaign goods for a nominal NT$40 shipping fee. Having clicked a transaction link and completed what was presented as real-name verification, she was told by a supposed vendor that her account had been frozen. An accomplice impersonating a bank employee then walked her through 32 online transactions, draining NT$1.39 million.

Another victim, keen to obtain a campaign umbrella, was coaxed by a bogus customer service representative into scanning a QR code and then generating one for a cardless withdrawal, losing upwards of NT$920,000. In both cases, the scammers relied on claims that an account was frozen or that a transaction needed to be verified.

The CIB emphasised that no legitimate purchase involves confirming payment through online banking, and urged the public to halt any transaction the moment a dubious link or banking request appears, and to consult the 165 anti-fraud hotline or its online dashboard.
sentZh: 台灣地方選舉已不到三週，警方警告，詐騙集團正趁著競選季節，以免費選舉周邊商品為誘餌，引誘毫無戒心的民眾落入精心設計的銀行詐騙。
刑事警察局（CIB）週日公布的數據顯示，過去兩個月選舉相關詐騙已讓受害者損失新台幣2015萬元。
損失大多發生在十月，當月87件案例共造成新台幣1911萬元損失。
在一個典型案例中，一名高雄老師看到一則社群媒體貼文，只需象徵性支付新台幣40元運費就能拿到免費競選商品。
她點了交易連結並完成所謂的實名認證後，一名自稱賣家的人告訴她帳戶已遭凍結。
接著一名冒充銀行員工的共犯一步步引導她完成32筆網路交易，騙走新台幣139萬元。
另一名受害者很想拿到競選雨傘，被假冒的客服代表哄騙掃描QR碼，再產生一組無卡提款碼，損失超過新台幣92萬元。

刑事局強調，任何正當的購物都不需要透過網路銀行確認付款，並呼籲民眾一旦出現可疑連結或銀行要求，就立刻中止交易，並諮詢165反詐騙專線或其線上資訊平台。

paragraphs: The run-up to an election is usually associated with rallies, debates and campaign flyers. In Taiwan, however, police say it has also become fertile ground for fraud, as criminals exploit public enthusiasm for free campaign merchandise ahead of local elections due in less than three weeks.

According to the Criminal Investigation Bureau (CIB), election-related scams have inflicted losses of NT$20.15 million over the past two months, with October alone accounting for 87 cases and NT$19.11 million. The figures suggest that the problem has escalated sharply as polling day approaches.

The method is deceptively simple. Victims are drawn in by online offers of free goods, such as umbrellas, in return for a token delivery fee. Once they have clicked a link or undergone a so-called real-name verification, a fraudster posing as the vendor claims their account has been frozen, and an accomplice impersonating bank staff or customer service persuades them to carry out online transfers, scan QR codes or set up cardless withdrawals. A teacher in Kaohsiung lost NT$1.39 million across 32 transactions, while another victim was defrauded of more than NT$920,000.
Such schemes succeed because they combine a trivial initial request with a manufactured sense of urgency, leaving victims little time to reflect.

The CIB's advice is unambiguous: legitimate transactions never require payment verification via online banking. Anyone confronted with a suspicious link or banking request should terminate the exchange at once and verify it through the 165 anti-fraud hotline.
sentZh: 選舉前夕通常讓人聯想到造勢集會、辯論會和競選傳單。
然而在台灣，警方表示這段時間也成了詐騙的溫床，因為罪犯利用民眾對免費競選商品的熱衷，在不到三週後的地方選舉前大肆行騙。
根據刑事警察局（CIB），過去兩個月選舉相關詐騙已造成新台幣2015萬元的損失，光是十月就占了87件案例、新台幣1911萬元。
這些數字顯示，隨著投票日接近，問題已急遽惡化。
這種手法看似簡單，實則暗藏玄機。
受害者被網路上的免費贈品（例如雨傘）吸引，只需付一筆象徵性的運費。
一旦他們點了連結或完成所謂的實名認證，冒充賣家的詐騙者就會聲稱他們的帳戶被凍結，接著假冒銀行人員或客服的共犯便說服他們進行網路轉帳、掃描QR碼或設定無卡提款。
高雄一名老師在32筆交易中損失新台幣139萬元，另一名受害者則被騙走超過新台幣92萬元。
這類騙局之所以得逞，是因為它們把微不足道的初步要求與刻意製造的緊迫感結合在一起，讓受害者幾乎沒有時間思考。
刑事局的建議非常明確：正當的交易絕不需要透過網路銀行驗證付款。
任何人遇到可疑連結或銀行要求，都應立即結束對話，並透過165反詐騙專線查證。

example.en: The fraudster posed as a bank employee on the phone.
example.zh: 詐騙犯在電話中冒充銀行員工。

note.meaning: 以欺騙手段騙取錢財的人。
note.usage: 英式用法較常見；美式常說 scammer / con artist。常接 posing as。

noteHi.exampleTr: धोखेबाज़ ने फ़ोन पर बैंक कर्मचारी होने का दिखावा किया।
noteHi.meaning: धोखे से पैसा ठगने वाला व्यक्ति।
noteHi.usage: ब्रिटिश अंग्रेज़ी में आम; fraudster posing as ... प्रयोग होता है।

noteEs.exampleTr: El estafador se hizo pasar por empleado del banco por teléfono.
noteEs.meaning: persona que engaña a otros para obtener dinero.
noteEs.usage: Más común en inglés británico; suele ir con posing as.

noteJa.exampleTr: 詐欺師は電話で銀行員になりすました。
noteJa.usage: イギリス英語で多い。fraudster posing as ～ の形でよく使う。

noteKo.usage: 영국 영어에서 흔함; fraudster posing as ~ 형태로 자주 쓴다.

noteEn.meaning: a person who tricks people to get money.
noteEn.usage: More common in British English; often 'a fraudster posing as ...'.

fraudsters.en: people who trick others to get money
